item.title: Apple's HomeView brings personalized Siri to smart home, takes on Amazon and Google
item.description: Apple on Tuesday unveiled a smart-home hub that taps iPhone user data to make Siri more personal, but promised privacy safeguards designed to keep that information out of the company's hands.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: Apple (AAPL.O) on Tuesday unveiled a smart-home hub that taps iPhone user data to make Siri more personal, but promised privacy safeguards designed to keep that information out of the company's hands. The HomeView smart-home hub, which [USN:L6N45Y122 TEXT:"took center stage"] at an event in New York, is an important test of Apple's AI strategy as it tries to close the gap with rivals Amazon (AMZN.O) and Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google, while reinforcing its reputation for user privacy. In a series of demonstrations, Apple showed Siri AI recognizing a user's face and performing personalized tasks such as fetching recipes from text messages, finding a nearby farmer's market for missing ingredients and then updating shopping lists. When a different member of the household steps in, the HomeView recognizes that user's face and switches to their personal data, for example fetching information from text messages about when a friend's early morning flight lands and how long it will take them to arrive, then teeing up a coffee maker a few minutes ahead of time. The new device and Siri AI lean on the iPhone to make those personalized features happen, reflecting new CEO John Ternus' vision of Apple's best-selling product as an "intelligent personal hub" laid out at Apple's iPhone launch [USN:L6N45206Y TEXT:"event last month"]. Siri AI's usefulness hinges on how much it knows about a user. HomeView draws on a personal search index stored on the user's iPhone to personalize responses. "That will give you what's more relevant, what's more timely, what's important to you, because it's coming from your iPhone," Kaiann Drance, Apple's vice president of product marketing for home products, said in an interview. PRIVACY SAFEGUARDS AND ENCRYPTION HomeView has its own operating system and runs on Apple's A18 chip, designed to process encrypted user data in a walled-off part of the chip. To access private data, a user's iPhone has to be connected to the same home network as HomeView, and no private data is stored on the HomeView device itself. Apple said none of the data is used for marketing, including first-party advertising efforts. "One of the things we talked about is not building a marketing profile," Drance said. "Our intent is to provide users a helpful experience that adheres to simplicity, being personal, being intelligent, and continuing our commitment to privacy." A key difference between Siri AI and rival systems is that it does not end each interaction with a follow-up question designed to elicit more information from the user, a practice that Lilian Rincon, vice president of product marketing for AI, said was a deliberate choice on Apple's part. "For us, it's really about creating these really great products for consumers, which is why we're not in this game of getting you to engage and continue the conversation in many, many, many turns," Rincon said. HomeView also required Apple to figure out how to make Siri personal on a device shared by multiple people in communal spaces such as a kitchen. Apple demonstrated HomeView juggling requests from family members during the morning rush to school and work. While the device can recognize up to six voices and faces to show private data, Apple said it will make decisions on which user to prioritize based on who last touched the device and other factors, and that some features such as weather and thermostat controls will be available to any user. "There is a logic built in to kind of manage that experience," Drance said. "There was thought put into the nature of that communal computer sharing of the voice and the face recognition."

item.title: US appeals court limits felon gun ban, allows for violent cases
item.description: A US appeals court concluded on Tuesday that a federal law barring felons from owning guns can only be constitutionally applied when a person's prior conviction involved violence or threats suggesting a risk of firearms misuse.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A US appeals court concluded on Tuesday that a federal law barring felons from owning guns can only be constitutionally applied when a person's prior conviction involved violence or threats suggesting a risk of firearms misuse. The full Philadelphia-based 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals in a pair of decisions ruled that in such cases, the primary federal law used to keep guns out of felons' hands does not violate the US Constitution's Second Amendment. The court, which now has a conservative majority following recent appointments by Republican President Donald Trump, said the law could be used to disarm a man convicted in a carjacking case but not against another man whose conviction stemmed from a DUI conviction. The decisions came in the latest in a series of court cases grappling with whether modern firearms restrictions remain valid after the Supreme Court handed down a landmark Second Amendment ruling in 2022 that expanded gun rights. The 6-3 conservative majority's [USN:L1N2YB1OL TEXT:"decision"], New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen, held that modern gun restrictions must be "consistent with this nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation." One of the cases before the 3rd Circuit concerned James Bost, who had pleaded guilty to terroristic threats and criminal conspiracy charges in Pennsylvania state court arising out of a 2002 carjacking. When he was later indicted for possessing a gun despite his convictions, he moved to dismiss the case, arguing the ban, which dates to the 1960s, ran afoul of his right to keep and bear arms under the Second Amendment. But US Circuit Judge Stephanos Bibas, writing for the majority in Bost's case, said individuals convicted of crimes like Bost's that demonstrate a risk of physical violence from misusing guns may presumptively be disarmed based on their convictions alone. "The right to keep and bear arms has limits, and this is one: Those who pose a risk of physical violence from misusing guns can be disarmed before that risk becomes a reality," wrote Bibas, a Trump appointee, for a 12-2 court. But the 3rd Circuit split 8-6 along ideological lines in the separate case of Edward Williams, who had two convictions for driving under the influence of alcohol in the early 2000s, including one that triggered the federal ban, which covers offenses that are punishable by at least one year in prison. Williams had been sentenced to 90 days to two years, which he served in home confinement. Upon learning the conviction barred him from owning guns, he sued in order to secure a declaration that the law was unconstitutional as applied to his offense. In a majority decision joined only by Republican-appointed judges, Trump-appointed US Circuit Judge Paul Matey agreed as he rejected the Justice Department's contention that historical laws targeting "habitual drunkards" showed the law fell within the nation's tradition of firearms regulation. Matey called Williams "a peaceable citizen, capable of bearing arms consistent with the design of the Second Amendment." "And with that rehabilitation comes restoration of the civic privileges guaranteed to citizens by the Constitution, and the freedom to again exercise the natural right of armed defense against threats and tyranny," he wrote. The six dissenting judges were all appointed by Democratic presidents, including US Circuit Judge Arianna Freeman, who said she parted ways "from the majority opinion when it says a prior conviction is disarming on its face only if it involved violence or threats." While convictions that require violence or threats certainly qualify, the judge said, so do other offenses, including for drunk driving, "that show a person poses a credible threat to the physical safety of others." The cases in the 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals are United States v Bost, No. 24-1719, and Williams v Attorney General, No. 24-1091. For the United States in Bost: Donovan Cocas of the US Attorney's Office for the Western District of Pennsylvania For the United States in Williams: Vivek Suri of the US Department of Justice For Bost: Jasmine R. Sola of the Federal Public Defender's Office for the Western District of Pennsylvania For Williams: Joshua Prince of Prince Law Offices

item.title: Bears DE Montez Sweat suspended 2 games for PED violation
item.description: The NFL suspended Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat two games without pay on Tuesday for a violation of its performance-enhancing substance policy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The NFL suspended Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat two games without pay on Tuesday for a violation of its performance-enhancing substance policy. Shemar Turner was activated off of the physically unable to perform list and replaces Sweat on the 53-man roster. The Bears had until Thursday to activate Turner, whose 21-day practice window opened Sept. 23. Sweat will miss the Bears' contest at the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday followed by a Thursday night home game against the New England Patriots. He would be eligible to return for Week 8, when the Bears visit the Seattle Seahawks on "Monday Night Football" Nov. 2. Sweat, 30, is a one-time Pro Bowler in his third full season with the Bears. He has two sacks through five games after compiling 10 sacks a year ago. Drafted in the first round (No. 26 overall) by Washington in 2019, Sweat was traded to the Bears in 2023, the year of his first and only Pro Bowl selection. Across 114 career games (all starts) with the two franchises, Sweat has amassed 59 sacks, 314 tackles (75 for loss), 133 quarterback hits, 15 forced fumbles, 21 pass breakups, and one interception. Turner has been working back from a torn ACL he suffered on Oct. 26, 2025. --Field Level Media

item.title: Funcionário da OpenAI é preso acusado de porte de dispositivo de escuta, diz empresa
item.description: A OpenAI anunciou nesta terça-feira que a polícia federal dos Estados Unidos (FBI) prendeu um de seus funcionários em conexão com um sofisticado dispositivo de escuta encontrado escondido em um dos escritórios da empresa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A OpenAI anunciou nesta terça-feira que a polícia federal dos Estados Unidos (FBI) prendeu um de seus funcionários em conexão com um sofisticado dispositivo de escuta encontrado escondido em um dos escritórios da empresa. A criadora do ChatGPT utilizou seus modelos internos de IA para identificar o indivíduo responsável por instalar o dispositivo e rastrear sua origem, informou a companhia na rede social X. “No momento, não temos indícios de que esse indivíduo tenha acessado indevidamente ou extraído modelos, código-fonte ou dados de clientes. O funcionário foi demitido”, afirmou a companhia de inteligência artificial. A OpenAI afirmou que seu programa de segurança foi projetado para proteger contra uma ampla gama de agentes de ameaças, desde riscos internos até criminosos externos e Estados-nação. A empresa disse que encaminhou o caso ao FBI, que continua investigando. A descoberta ocorre em um momento em que a OpenAI enfrenta críticas sobre incidentes de segurança envolvendo seus sistemas de IA. No início deste mês, a Reuters e outros veículos de comunicação noticiaram que a OpenAI informou aos investidores que sua receita anualizada para setembro era de quase US$50 bilhões, uma queda em relação ao que havia sido sinalizado anteriormente. (Por Jaspreet Singh)

item.title: Activist investor Ancora pushes Big Yellow to explore sale
item.description: Activist investor Ancora Holdings has urged Britain-listed Big Yellow Group to launch a strategic review, including a potential sale of the self-storage company.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Activist investor Ancora Holdings has urged Britain-listed Big Yellow Group (BYG.L) to launch a strategic review, including a potential sale of the self-storage company. A sale represents the best risk-adjusted outcome for shareholders, Ancora, which has a more than 4% stake in Big Yellow, said in a presentation on Tuesday. Ancora said Big Yellow shares, which have fallen 23.6% so far this year, trade at an "unwarranted" discount to net asset value Big Yellow did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment Ancora estimates Big Yellow is worth £12.36 ($16.38) per share; Its shares closed at £7.99 on Tuesday, giving the company a market value of about £1.6 billion Ancora's push comes nearly a year after Big Yellow terminated discussions with Blackstone (BX.N) for a takeover at an undisclosed offer price Ancora said on Tuesday Blackstone had offered Big Yellow 50% above the current stock price and that if the company were to solicit interest from parties now, a deal could likely occur at a valuation above what Blackstone offered Blackstone did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on its 2025 offer for Big Yellow Big Yellow is "an attractive asset for both financial sponsors and strategic acquirers given the company's relative cheapness" compared to US storage REITs and the "scarcity value" of its UK portfolio, Ancora said Ancora is among a growing number of activists pressing companies to pursue asset sales or takeovers as M&A activity rebounds and pressure mounts on boards to unlock shareholder value. It had in June urged specialty chemicals maker Ashland (ASH.N) to [USN:L1N42H0S6 TEXT:"explore a sale"] ($1 = 0.7545 pounds)

item.title: Mexicano Grupo Televisa comprará filial de AT&T en México por 2,000 mln dlr
item.description: El mexicano Grupo Televisa anunció el martes que un consorcio que integra junto con Fintech Holdings Inc. alcanzó un acuerdo con AT&T para adquirir su filial en México por 2,000 millones de dólares.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El mexicano Grupo Televisa anunció el martes que un consorcio que integra junto con Fintech Holdings Inc. alcanzó un acuerdo con AT&T para adquirir su filial en México por 2,000 millones de dólares. Televisa (TLEVISACPO.MX) dijo que el consorcio espera financiar la adquisición de negocio de AT&T (T.N) a través de una combinación de efectivo disponible y un financiamiento de deuda garantizada. Televisa dijo que AT&T México es el segundo más grande operador móvil en México, con aproximadamente 24.7 millones de suscriptores al 31 de diciembre de 2025, y provee servicios integrados de telecomunicaciones incluyendo telefonía móvil, internet, y servicios de valor agregado Se espera que la transacción, sujeta a la obtención de aprobaciones regulatorias, se cierre en el primer trimestre de 2027. Las acciones de Televisa cerraron el martes antes del anuncio en 8.10 pesos en la bolsa local, una pérdida del 0.49%. Los títulos de AT&T cerraron con un alza del 1.60% en el NYSE, a 22.85 dólares, también antes de la noticia.

item.title: TRADING DAY Earnings season debuts to mixed reviews
item.description: Wall Street stocks were muted on Tuesday after big banks reported mixed earnings and investors looked ahead to Wednesday's crucial inflation report. The S&P 500 ended essentially flat, while Nasdaq closed slightly lower, weighed by chip weakness.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp
item.content:encoded: Wall Street stocks were muted on Tuesday after big banks reported mixed earnings and investors looked ahead to Wednesday's crucial inflation report. The S&P 500 ended essentially flat, while Nasdaq closed slightly lower, weighed by chip weakness. Third-quarter earnings optimism has been propping up the market, helping it soldier through geopolitical turmoil, surging bond yields and mounting inflation worries. Analysts currently expect year-on-year S&P 500 earnings growth of 30.6% for the July-September period, according to LSEG data. I will go into more detail on today's market moves below. item.title: Nneka Ogwumike wins sportsmanship honor for fifth time
item.description: Los Angeles Sparks forward Nneka Ogwumike was named winner of the Kim Perrot Sportsmanship Award on Tuesday, extending her record for winning the award to five times.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Sparks forward Nneka Ogwumike was named winner of the Kim Perrot Sportsmanship Award on Tuesday, extending her record for winning the award to five times. This marks the second straight season in which the 36-year-old Ogwumike won the award. She previously won it three straight times from 2019-21. Ogwumike previously announced the 2026 season would be her 15th and final campaign. She averaged 17.3 points, 9.0 rebounds and 3.1 assists in 43 games this season. Ogwumike received 38 votes in balloting of a panel of 74 sportswriters and broadcasters. Rebecca Allen (seven) of the New York Liberty was second and Kelsey Mitchell (six) of the Indiana Fever placed third. Ogwumike finished her career ranked fourth in WNBA history in points (8,047) and steals (718) and third in rebounds (3,657). She was an 11-time All-Star while playing for the Sparks (2012-23, 2026) and Seattle Storm (2024-25) and was league MVP in 2016 while leading Los Angeles to the WNBA title. The award is named after Kim Perrot, who won two WNBA championships with the Houston Comets (1997-98) before passing away in August 1999 after a battle with cancer. She was 32. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ex-líder de gangue é condenado à prisão perpétua pelo assassinato de Tupac Shakur
item.description: Um ex-líder de gangue foi condenado nesta terça-feira a uma pena de prisão perpétua, com possibilidade de condicional após cumprir 40 anos, por orquestrar o assassinato do astro do hip-hop Tupac Shakur, ocorrido em 1996 em Las Vegas, encerrando o processo judicial do homicídio há muito não resolvido que marcou a era de ouro do rap.
item.dc:creator: Jack Queen, Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: Um ex-líder de gangue foi condenado nesta terça-feira a uma pena de prisão perpétua, com possibilidade de condicional após cumprir 40 anos, por orquestrar o assassinato do astro do hip-hop Tupac Shakur, ocorrido em 1996 em Las Vegas, encerrando o processo judicial do homicídio há muito não resolvido que marcou a era de ouro do rap. Duane “Keffe D” Davis, de 63 anos, considerado culpado de homicídio doloso em agosto, recebeu a sentença durante uma audiência nesta terça em um tribunal de Las Vegas. Em depoimento emocionado perante a juíza Carli Kierny, a irmã mais nova de Shakur, Sekyiwa Shakur, disse que sua mãe o criou para ser um ativista dos direitos humanos e o tratava como se ele tivesse o potencial de mudar o mundo. “Ele acreditava nela”, disse Sekyiwa Shakur, vestindo uma blusa preta. “Ele saiu pelo mundo para fazer isso. E acredito que ele teria conseguido.” Até a prisão de Davis em 2023, o assassinato de Shakur -- morto a tiros no banco do passageiro de um SUV dirigido por seu executivo da gravadora, Marion “Suge” Knight -- permaneceu por quase três décadas como um dos casos não resolvidos mais notórios dos Estados Unidos. O assassinato, que silenciou um dos artistas de rap mais influentes e bem-sucedidos comercialmente, reforçou a imagem de violência que permeava a cultura hip-hop dos anos 1990, ao mesmo tempo em que alimentava a infame rivalidade entre o rap “gangsta” da Costa Leste e da Costa Oeste dos EUA na época. Apesar da condenação de Davis, a questão de quem puxou o gatilho no disparo fatal contra a lenda do rap de 25 anos nunca foi decidida de forma conclusiva. Davis foi julgado e condenado por planejar o assassinato para vingar a agressão sofrida por seu sobrinho por parte de Shakur e membros da comitiva do rapper dentro do cassino MGM Grand, na Las Vegas Strip, em 7 de setembro de 1996. Davis afirmou que deve recorrer da condenação. MUNDO NUNCA ESQUECEU Autoridades afirmaram que acreditavam no envolvimento de Davis, mas não tinham provas suficientes para acusá-lo. Isso mudou quando ele tornou pública sua versão dos fatos em aparições na mídia e em um livro de memórias que, juntamente com gravações de suas reuniões secretas com os investigadores, constituiu a maior parte do processo de homicídio da acusação. Em seu livro, “Compton Street Legend”, o próprio Davis escreveu que era considerado suspeito dos assassinatos tanto de Shakur quanto de Christopher Wallace, um rapper rival. Dirigindo-se a Davis nesta terça-feira, a juíza disse que suas alegações de que ele havia mudado desde a década de 1990 não eram suficientes. “Você não tem o direito de tirar um homem de sua família”, disse Kierny, referindo-se a Shakur. “O mundo nunca se esqueceu dele.” BRIGA EM CASSINO O confronto no cassino teve origem na hostilidade entre duas gangues de rua da região de Los Angeles -- os South Side Compton Crips, dos quais Davis se autodenominava líder, e os Mob Piru, associados a Shakur, Knight e sua gravadora, a Death Row Records. Membros dos dois grupos estavam em Las Vegas para assistir, naquela noite, a uma luta pelo título mundial de boxe na categoria peso-pesado entre Mike Tyson e Bruce Seldon. Poucas horas após a briga no cassino, Davis colocou seu sobrinho e dois outros comparsas em um Cadillac branco e saiu em busca de Shakur e Knight, determinado a acertar as contas, de acordo com um depoimento prestado por Davis à polícia em uma investigação posterior não relacionada ao caso, mas citada pelos promotores durante o julgamento por homicídio. Davis disse que passou uma arma para os dois homens sentados atrás dele no Cadillac, um dos quais responsável por disparar pela janela quando se colocaram ao lado do veículo de Knight e Shakur no trânsito. Shakur foi atingido quatro vezes e morreu em um hospital seis dias depois. Knight, que sofreu um ferimento leve causado por um fragmento de bala que lhe raspou a cabeça, cumpre atualmente uma pena de 28 anos de prisão por uma condenação não relacionada por homicídio doloso. Embora Davis nunca tenha sido acusado de realmente disparar os tiros que mataram Shakur -- a lei de Nevada permite que alguém seja acusado de homicídio por participação no crime --, os promotores nunca identificaram um suspeito de ter disparado. Todos os outros três homens que estavam no Cadillac com Davis naquela noite já faleceram.

item.title: Report: Celtics sign G Payton Pritchard to 2-year, $44.2M extension
item.description: The Boston Celtics agreed to a two-year, $44.2-million contract extension with guard Payton Pritchard that will begin in the 2028-29 season, ESPN reported Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Boston Celtics agreed to a two-year, $44.2-million contract extension with guard Payton Pritchard that will begin in the 2028-29 season, ESPN reported Tuesday. Pritchard, 28, delivered the best season of his six-year career in 2025-26 when he averaged career bests with 17.0 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds. He played in 79 games while making 50 starts after making 17 total starts over his first five seasons. The deal for the 2024-25 Sixth Man of the Year, includes a mutual option for the 2029-30 season. His current deal in Boston runs through the 2027-28 season. A first-round draft pick (26th overall) by the Celtics in 2020 out of Oregon, Pritchard has averaged 10.6 points with 3.0 assists and 3.0 rebounds in 426 games (67 starts) all in Boston. During the Celtics' run to the NBA title in 2024, Pritchard averaged 6.4 points with 2.1 assists and 1.9 rebounds in 19 playoff games. --Field Level Media

item.title: OpenAI hit with proposed class action over collection of children’s data
item.description: OpenAI illegally profits from the personal information and data minors share with ChatGPT, a mother whose two children use the chatbot alleged in a proposed class action filed in San Francisco federal court on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: OpenAI illegally profits from the personal information and data minors share with ChatGPT, a mother whose two children use the chatbot alleged in a proposed class action filed in San Francisco federal court on Tuesday. • The lawsuit, filed on behalf of minors who have used ChatGPT, claims the chatbot is designed to collect data and information from minors, which is then used to train OpenAI's AI models • The chatbot elicits information about personal problems from minors in chats full of emojis and slang that kids use • Minors can’t consent to the use of their data under California law, lawsuit claims • Lawsuit wants OpenAI equity awarded to minors who use ChatGPT and a declaration that the site's terms of use are void for minors • A representative for OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but on its website the company says that it gives users control over whether their data is available to train other AI models • The lawsuit comes after a series of cases against OpenAI that [USN:L6N45K0T3 TEXT:"have"] [USN:L6N45D0ZP TEXT:"been"] [USN:L6N43O111 TEXT:"filed"] in US state and federal courts in recent months over claims that ChatGPT facilitated violence The case is Jane Doe et al v. OpenAI Foundation et al, US District Court for the Northern District of California, case number 3:26-cv-11781. For plaintiffs: R. Paul Yetter of Yetter Coleman For OpenAI: unavailable

item.title: Bank of England's Bailey says companies are focusing on costs
item.description: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said companies in Britain are focusing intensely on containing their costs amid the surge in energy prices caused by the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said companies in Britain are focusing intensely on containing their costs amid the surge in energy prices caused by the Iran war . In an interview with CNN broadcast on Tuesday, Bailey reiterated his previous comments that pressure on broader inflation in the UK from the energy shock had so far been subdued, "but the longer this goes on, the harder it gets." While the BoE would take into consideration the resilience to date of the UK economy, Bailey said there were signs of companies taking a cautious stance. "When I go around the country — and I do a lot of talking to firms, and my colleagues do — there's a very big focus on cost containment in terms of when they're looking at the increase in their costs," he said. A focus on cost-cutting could affect the labour market, although it was still "early days" for assessing the impact of the energy price surge in areas such as wages, Bailey added. The BoE has kept borrowing costs on hold since the start of the Iran war, unlike the European Central Bank and the US Federal Reserve, which have both raised rates. However, investors are pricing the chance of a quarter-point rate hike by the BoE next month as a near certainty.

item.title: Watkins on target to keep Al-Hilal perfect in Asian Champions League
item.description: Al-Hilal secured a 2-0 win over Qatar's Al-Sadd in Doha on Tuesday with Ollie Watkins' improvised finish sending the Saudi Pro League outfit on their way to a second successive Asian Champions League Elite win.
item.dc:creator: Michael Church
item.content:encoded: Al-Hilal secured a 2-0 win over Qatar's Al-Sadd in Doha on Tuesday with Ollie Watkins' improvised finish sending the Saudi Pro League outfit on their way to a second successive Asian Champions League Elite win. The former Aston Villa striker netted in the 40th minute to give Al-Hilal the lead, calmly steering the ball home while lying on the turf after being upended in the penalty area by Agustin Soria. "I felt like I worked hard for the team, I got my goal and that's what I'm here to do, get goals for the team and ultimately work hard and put everything into the game," said Watkins. The win followed Al-Hilal's opening victory over Al-Gharafa in the western league phase of the competition last month and was sealed when Ruben Neves scored from the penalty spot in the 65th minute. Al-Hilal were joined on six points by Shabab Al-Ahli after the side from the United Arab Emirates beat former champions Al-Ittihad 2-1 in Jeddah. Sardar Azmoun struck twice in the opening 16 minutes, converting from close range in the seventh before the Iran international ran from just inside the Al-Ittihad half before finishing. Richard Rios pulled one back for the hosts in the 66th minute but Shabab Al-Ahli held on to take the points. "We were very focused and we believed we can win this game," said Azmoun. "We analysed them well and we worked on the pitch very hard and that's why we won the game." Al-Ain from the UAE and Iran's Esteghlal also have perfect records after two rounds of the eight-match league phase. The top eight finishers in both the west and east regions advance to the last 16.

item.title: Petrolera estadounidense NABEP dice que recibió dos taladros en Venezuela
item.description: La empresa energética estadounidense NABEP, que recientemente anunció una asociación con el gobierno de Estados Unidos para operar en Venezuela, informó el martes que la semana pasada recibió dos taladros de perforación en el país sudamericano, los cuales contribuirán a aumentar la producción.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La empresa energética estadounidense NABEP, que recientemente anunció una asociación con el gobierno de Estados Unidos para operar en Venezuela, informó el martes que la semana pasada recibió dos taladros de perforación en el país sudamericano, los cuales contribuirán a aumentar la producción. Asimismo, está desplegando en el país otros 11 equipos nuevos de reacondicionamiento de pozos de 550 caballos de fuerza, según indicó la compañía en un comunicado, añadiendo que ha adquirido por separado 60 equipos, 30 calderas de vapor y 70 unidades de maquinaria pesada para ampliar su flota en la región. "NABEP está logrando avances serios y constantes en el aumento de la producción petrolera. Cada equipo que llega a Venezuela nos acerca más a alcanzar nuestras metas de producción y a revitalizar la economía del país", declaró el director ejecutivo de NABEP, el empresario venezolano Alejandro Betancourt.

item.title: Zealand Pharma, Generate strike AI obesity drug deal worth up to $1.2 billion
item.description: Zealand Pharma and Generate Biomedicines said on Tuesday they have partnered to develop protein-based treatments for obesity and other metabolic diseases using AI, in a deal worth up to nearly $1.2 billion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zealand Pharma (ZELA.CO) and Generate Biomedicines (GENB.O) said on Tuesday they have partnered to develop protein-based treatments for obesity and other metabolic diseases using AI, in a deal worth up to nearly $1.2 billion. Shares of Somerville, Massachusetts-based Generate Biomedicines were up about 5% in extended trading. Generate will receive $30 million upfront and up to $35 million in early preclinical milestones and could earn nearly $1.2 billion in development, regulatory and commercial milestones, the companies said. Generate will lead research through lead-candidate selection, while Zealand will oversee clinical development, regulatory submissions and commercialization.

item.title: Bank of America fined $1.2 billion by US government for failing to police suspicious activity
item.description: Bank of America has been fined $1.21 billion by the US government for what it called widespread failures to properly police potential money laundering and other illicit activity at the nation's second-largest bank.
item.dc:creator: Pete Schroeder, Ismail Shakil, Saeed Azhar
item.content:encoded: Bank of America (BAC.N) has been fined $1.21 billion by the US government for what it called widespread failures to properly police potential money laundering and other illicit activity at the nation's second-largest bank. The Treasury Department said the fine, the third-largest in department history, is due to the bank's failure to report over $5 billion in suspicious activity to the government, including $1 billion in activity that posed national security-related and other priority illicit finance risks. “Financial institutions are on the front lines of protecting our economic and national security,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in a statement. “When a bank of this size fails to meet its anti-money laundering and sanctions obligations, the consequences extend far beyond its own walls, exposing the entire US financial system to significant illicit finance risks." The Treasury said the bank "prioritized its revenues" in building compliance programs, and overly relied on inquiries from outside parties like law enforcement and other financial institutions instead of its own internal controls. “Financial crime compliance is serious, and we are responsible for getting it right," said a Bank of America spokesperson in a statement. "We have invested billions of dollars in technology and dedicated thousands of employees to combat financial crime, and our team is far along with and committed to completing the work required to address the issues raised by our regulators." The spokesperson added that the bank's third-quarter results due for release on Wednesday will include a non-tax-deductible charge of $1.2 billion, which will reduce quarterly net income by approximately 17 cents a share. Shares were down 1.8% in after-hours trading. As part of the fine, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency levied a $750 million civil penalty against the lender, the largest ever for the regulator, citing failures to address shortcomings in its anti-money laundering programs that were identified as part of a 2024 cease-and-desist order from the watchdog. The regulator said the bank's compliance program was "deficient and ineffective," and its transaction monitoring system caused the bank to delay in filing suspicious activity reports on billions of dollars of transactions. In addition, the bank paid an $11.6 million fine to the Office of Foreign Assets Control for over 400 apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs. The Treasury said the bank mistakenly processed millions of dollars in payments that violated sanctions programs targeting countries including Russia and Iran. The fine comes days after American Express [USN:L6N45U1AT TEXT:"was also hit with a $350 million penalty"] for similar anti-money laundering shortcomings.

item.title: Nasdaq fecha em baixa com queda das fabricantes de chips e divulgação de resultados de bancos
item.description: O Nasdaq fechou em baixa nesta terça-feira, com as ações do setor de chips ampliando as perdas recentes e os investidores analisando os resultados trimestrais mistos do Citigroup e de outros grandes bancos dos EUA.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: O Nasdaq fechou em baixa nesta terça-feira, com as ações do setor de chips ampliando as perdas recentes e os investidores analisando os resultados trimestrais mistos do Citigroup e de outros grandes bancos dos EUA. O índice de chips da PHLX (.SOX) caiu 0,23%, queda pela quinta sessão consecutiva, depois que o presidente-executivo da Broadcom (AVGO.O) , Hock Tan, comparou na segunda-feira parte do fluxo de investimentos no setor a “apostas em cassinos”. Além disso, reportagens sobre avanços tecnológicos da empresa chinesa de chips de memória CXMT reforçaram as preocupações com o aumento da concorrência. A Micron Technology (MU.O) perdeu 3,6% e a Applied Materials (AMAT.O) tombou quase 7%. A Broadcom subiu 0,7%. O Citigroup (C.N) tombou 5,6% e o Goldman Sachs (GS.N) perdeu 0,2% depois que ambos os bancos superaram as estimativas de lucro. O Wells Fargo (WFC.N) caiu 3,1% depois que sua margem financeira líquida ficou abaixo das estimativas, enquanto o JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) encerrou o dia com queda de 0,9% após um raro resultado abaixo do esperado. A Apple (AAPL.O) atingiu uma alta recorde intradia de US$348,15 antes de fechar com alta de 0,1%, a US$341,27, elevando seu valor de mercado para US$4,98 trilhões. Analistas preveem, em média, que os lucros do terceiro trimestre do S&P 500 cresçam mais de 30%, impulsionados em grande parte por empresas de tecnologia relacionadas à IA, de acordo com dados da LSEG. As expectativas de uma forte temporada de resultados compensaram as preocupações com a guerra dos EUA contra o Irã, o aumento dos rendimentos dos títulos e a inflação relacionada aos altos preços do petróleo. “Muitos investidores estão sentindo um alívio, pois os mercados podem começar a se concentrar mais nos lucros e menos no mercado de títulos, menos nos preços do petróleo mais altos por mais tempo e menos nas altas taxas de juros”, disse Jake Dollarhide, presidente-executivo da Longbow Asset Management em Tulsa, Oklahoma. O S&P 500 teve variação negativa de 0,02%, encerrando o pregão em 7.805,45 pontos. O Nasdaq recuou 0,15%, para 27.204,38 pontos, enquanto o Dow Jones Industrial Average caiu 0,35%, para 51.670,10 pontos. O S&P 500 acumula alta de 14% em 2026, impulsionado pelas ações de tecnologia relacionadas à IA. No entanto, a mediana das ações do índice subiu menos de 5% e mais de 200 componentes do S&P 500 apresentam queda no ano. O índice de chips PHLX perdeu mais de 8% nas últimas cinco sessões, mas continua com alta de mais de 70% no acumulado do ano. O índice de saúde do S&P 500 (.SPXHC) caiu 1,3% nesta terça-feira, com a Johnson & Johnson (JNJ.N) registrando queda de 5,7%, apesar de ter superado as estimativas de lucro. A Bumble (BMBL.O) disparou quase 57% depois que a operadora do aplicativo de namoro concordou em fechar seu capital em um negócio de US$1,3 bilhão. A Domino’s Pizza (DPZ.O) registrou queda de 4,8% após revisar para baixo sua previsão de vendas para o ano inteiro.

item.title: León se sometió a la extirpación de un lóbulo pulmonar tras diagnóstico de cáncer, dice el Vaticano
item.description: El papa León se sometió el martes a una intervención quirúrgica en la que se le extirpó el lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho y se le diagnosticó un adenocarcinoma pulmonar, un tipo común de cáncer de pulmón, informó el Vaticano en un boletín médico.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El papa León se sometió el martes a una intervención quirúrgica en la que se le extirpó el lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho y se le diagnosticó un adenocarcinoma pulmonar, un tipo común de cáncer de pulmón, informó el Vaticano en un boletín médico. León, de 71 años, ingresó el martes en el hospital Gemelli de Roma para someterse a una intervención quirúrgica destinada a extirpar un nódulo pulmonar que los médicos le detectaron en un reciente reconocimiento médico. La intervención quirúrgica del martes duró unos 90 minutos y se desarrolló con éxito, sin complicaciones, según informó el Vaticano. El papa se despertó con normalidad y está descansando en su habitación del hospital. El Vaticano había indicado anteriormente que se esperaba que el papa pasara una semana en el hospital recuperándose.

item.title: AT&T sells Mexico unit to Televisa, Fintech for $2 billion
item.description: US carrier AT&T on Tuesday said it has agreed to sell its Mexican unit to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2 billion in cash, as it sharpens its focus on domestic fiber and 5G networks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US carrier AT&T (T.N) on Tuesday said it has agreed to sell its Mexican unit to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2 billion in cash, as it sharpens its focus on domestic fiber and 5G networks. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, pending regulatory approvals in Mexico, AT&T said in a statement. Its Mexican unit, the country's second-largest mobile operator, had approximately 24.7 million subscribers as of December 2025, according to Televisa. The deal's purchase price of $2 billion in cash is subject to adjustments, plus additional contractual and contingent benefits, and will be funded through available cash and non-recourse secured debt financing. Televisa and Fintech each own a 50% stake of the consortium that is purchasing AT&T. AT&T Mexico reported revenues of 85.4 billion pesos and operating income of 1.4 billion pesos for 2025, Televisa said in its statement. AT&T will classify AT&T Mexico as held-for-sale in continuing operations in its third-quarter 2026 SEC filing. "We have articulated a strong belief that the AI future will run on converged networks with dense fiber assets," AT&T Chairman and CEO John Stankey said in a statement. "This move positions AT&T Mexico to participate in that evolution."

item.title: Papa Leão teve lobo do pulmão removido após médicos detectarem câncer, diz Vaticano
item.description: O papa Leão foi diagnosticado com uma forma comum de câncer de pulmão depois que os médicos removeram o lobo inferior do pulmão direito durante uma cirurgia realizada nesta terça-feira, informou o Vaticano em um boletim médico.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee, Matteo Negri
item.content:encoded: O papa Leão foi diagnosticado com uma forma comum de câncer de pulmão depois que os médicos removeram o lobo inferior do pulmão direito durante uma cirurgia realizada nesta terça-feira, informou o Vaticano em um boletim médico. O pontífice, de 71 anos, tem adenocarcinoma pulmonar. Exames de tecido realizados durante a operação confirmaram o que os médicos já suspeitavam com base nos exames preparatórios, informou o boletim. Leão, de 71 anos, foi internado no Hospital Gemelli, em Roma, nesta terça-feira, para uma cirurgia destinada a remover um nódulo no pulmão que os médicos detectaram em um exame médico recente. O Vaticano havia informado na noite desta terça-feira que a cirurgia havia sido bem-sucedida, antes de divulgar uma atualização mais detalhada do cirurgião-chefe do papa, o professor Stefano Margaritora, chefe de cirurgia torácica do Gemelli. “Para que o procedimento fosse curativo, o lobo inferior do pulmão direito foi removido por meio de uma técnica assistida por vídeo”, informou Margaritora em seu comunicado. “Um rápido exame histológico intraoperatório confirmou o diagnóstico de adenocarcinoma pulmonar, conforme já se suspeitava com base nos exames pré-operatórios”, acrescentou. A cirurgia realizada nesta terça-feira durou cerca de 90 minutos e foi bem-sucedida, sem complicações, informou o Vaticano. O papa acordou normalmente e está descansando em seu quarto no hospital. O comunicado não forneceu mais detalhes. PREVISÃO DE PERMANÊNCIA NO HOSPITAL POR UMA SEMANA Leão deixou o Vaticano antes da cirurgia, pouco antes das 13h em Roma, e foi visto acenando da parte de trás de um SUV preto enquanto sua comitiva dirigia cerca de 9 km ao norte do Vaticano, em direção ao Gemelli. Ao chegar ao hospital, Leão apertou a mão de várias autoridades, passou diante de uma multidão de simpatizantes que o aguardava — alguns dos quais gritavam “Auguri” (melhores votos) — e entrou pela entrada principal. O Vaticano informou no início desta semana que o papa deveria passar cerca de uma semana em recuperação no hospital. Todos os seus compromissos públicos foram cancelados até 20 de outubro. Leão, eleito pelos cardeais de todo o mundo em maio de 2025, é relativamente jovem para um líder da Igreja. Ele gosta de esportes, incluindo tênis, e não é conhecido por ser fumante nem por ter tido problemas de saúde recentes. O falecido papa Francisco, predecessor de Leão, foi hospitalizado várias vezes à medida que sua saúde se debilitava nos últimos anos de vida. Ele faleceu aos 88 anos em abril de 2025. Leão, que falou com voz firme e clara em seu único evento público na segunda-feira, mantém uma agenda muito ocupada. Ele deve realizar uma viagem de 11 dias pelo Uruguai, Argentina e Peru, de 6 a 17 de novembro. FEBRE TIFOIDE O papa é a máxima autoridade terrena para os 1,4 bilhão de católicos do mundo e não tem um substituto que assuma suas funções quando ele fica doente. Quando um papa fica incapacitado, os trabalhos da vasta burocracia do Vaticano seguem normalmente, adiando quaisquer decisões que exijam aprovação papal. Leão, nascido em Chicago em 1955 como Robert Prevost, atuou por décadas como missionário e bispo no Peru antes de se tornar papa. Em 1985, quando era um jovem padre, contraiu febre tifoide em Chulucanas, no Peru, e foi hospitalizado. Ele relatou a experiência em sua única grande entrevista concedida como papa, em um livro publicado pela Penguin Peru. Leão disse que a dor era tão forte que pediu a Deus para morrer, em vez de continuar sofrendo. Ele interpretou sua sobrevivência como um sinal de Deus de que “precisamos de você aqui (na Terra)”, disse ele. “Nunca mais olhei para trás”, disse Leão.

item.title: Cornell bans fraternity parties for rest of academic year after alleged gang rape
item.description: The measure is the strongest reaction yet from Cornell's leadership to a lawsuit filed by a former undergraduate, Jane Doe, alleging that seven men sexually assaulted her during a party two years ago.
item.dc:creator: Maria Tsvetkova
item.content:encoded: Cornell University will ban parties and social events at fraternity houses until the end of the academic year, its president said on Tuesday, responding to the outcry over an alleged gang rape on campus in 2024. The measure is the strongest reaction yet from Cornell's leadership to a lawsuit filed by a former undergraduate, Jane Doe, alleging that seven men sexually assaulted her during a party two years ago. Over the last several weeks, the Ivy League school in Ithaca, New York, and its president, Michael Kotlikoff, have come under heavy criticism from students, faculty and donors over its response to the allegations. The suspension of parties and social events will apply to Interfraternity Council houses. The Council website says Cornell currently has 34 fraternity houses. "These measures will provide time for a thorough review of fraternity life at Cornell to determine whether and how it can safely continue," Kotlikoff said in the statement. The Cornell Interfraternity Council did not immediately reply to a request for comment. Since the [USN:L1N45K0ML TEXT:"lawsuit"] against seven fraternity members, the university and others was filed in September, the Cornell administration has faced student protests, a pending no-confidence resolution from faculty, criticism by alumni and a public assembly where students blamed university officials for tolerating what they described as a culture of sexual violence. None of the men named in the lawsuit have been criminally charged. "I have spent the past weeks listening to students, faculty, staff, parents, alumni, and trustees, who have shared their feelings of deep connection and sympathy with Jane Doe, anger and frustration that this could happen at Cornell," Kotlikoff said. "Women on our campus continue to question whether they are safe," he said, adding that additional staff would be hired to support survivors of sexual assault. Cornell will also work with New York State Police to investigate incidents, he said, and accelerate previous recommendations put forward by a task force on sexual violence. Thirty-five percent of undergraduate women reported experiencing non-consensual sexual contact involving force or incapacitation since entering Cornell, according to a university survey conducted in 2025 and published on its website. "We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short and taking meaningful action," Kotlikoff said.

item.title: Pope Leo had lobe of lung removed as doctors found cancer, Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo had a lower lobe of his right lung removed during surgery on Tuesday and was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pope Leo had a lower lobe of his right lung removed during surgery on Tuesday and was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin. Leo, 71, was admitted to Rome's Gemelli hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove a growth on his lung that doctors found in a recent health checkup. Tuesday's surgery lasted about 90 minutes and was successful with no complications, the Vatican said. The pope has woken up normally and is resting in his hospital room. The Vatican said previously that the pope was expected to spend a week in hospital recovering.

item.title: Galeão deve receber investimentos de R$1 bi nos próximos 3 anos
item.description: O aeroporto internacional do Rio de Janeiro, Galeão, deve receber investimentos privados de ao menos R$1 bilhão nos próximos três anos, disse o presidente no Brasil da nova concessionária do terminal, a espanhola Aena , Santiago Yus, nesta terça-feira.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Viga Gaier
item.content:encoded: O aeroporto internacional do Rio de Janeiro, Galeão, deve receber investimentos privados de ao menos R$1 bilhão nos próximos três anos, disse o presidente no Brasil da nova concessionária do terminal, a espanhola Aena (AENA.MC) , Santiago Yus, nesta terça-feira. Segundo ele, esses investimentos incluem um novo hotel de bandeira internacional com mais de 200 quartos, centro de testes da montadora BYD (002594.SZ) , novos hangares e galpões e um novo terminal de cargas. Os investimentos não contemplam futuros aportes Aena que assumiu oficialmente o controle do terminal na semana passada. O Galeão deve fechar o ano com um novo fluxo recorde de passageiros podendo alcançar 19 milhões de pessoas ante 17 milhões em 2025. Ainda sim, está longe da capacidade total que beira os 37 milhões de passageiros por ano. "No mundo trabalhamos com mais de 200 companhias aéreas e achamos que temos condições de trazer mais empresas para cá, ampliando frequências e destinos", afirmou o presidente da Aena no Brasil. O crescimento nos passageiros que passam pelo Galeão ocorre após o governo federal criar um teto de voos no aeroporto Santos Dumont, provocando uma migração de voos para o terminal internacional que antes da medida chegou a ter menos passageiros que o Santos Dumont. A flexibilização do teto de 6,5 milhões de passageiros para o Santos Dumont está em discussão pelo governo federal. O terminal na região central do Rio de Janeiro é a principal fonte de recursos da Infraero, estatal aeroportuária do governo federal. Uma futura concessão do Santos Dumont será analisada pela Aena, disse Yus. "Para a Aena, o Brasil é um mercado estratégico...então interesse (no Santos Dumont) no mínimo existirá", afirmou. A empresa de origem espanhola já administra 18 aeroportos no Brasil sendo Galeão e Congonhas, em São Paulo, os de maior destaque.

item.title: Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua bout could start after 1 a.m. in Wales
item.description: A request to hold the much-anticipated heavyweight bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in the very early morning hours has been filed in Cardiff, Wales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A request to hold the much-anticipated heavyweight bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in the very early morning hours has been filed in Cardiff, Wales. If approved, the bout would have a ring walk of 1 a.m. local time on Dec. 12, which equates to 8 p.m. on the East Coast of the United States and 5 p.m. on the West Coast on Dec. 11. The 74,000-seat Principality Stadium, home to the Wales national rugby team, is set to host the bout. Both Fury and Joshua have different stipulations as to where the bout can take place, with Cardiff working out as a compromise after locations like Dublin, Las Vegas and New York also were considered, The Athletic reported. Fury, 38, is from Manchester, England, while Joshua, 36, is from Watford, Hertfordshire, England. Cardiff requires boxing and wrestling events to end by 1 a.m., with the request asking for an extension until 3 a.m., with the stadium open until 3:30 a.m. A request to serve alcohol into the early-morning hours also has been submitted. Netflix is set to broadcast the bout, which was announced in September. Elected officials, as well as members of the public, have until Nov. 3 to give their opinion on the time extension to the Cardiff Council. --Field Level Media

item.title: Federal Circuit rejects PTAB's 'ministerial' requirement for prior art priority
item.description: Jonathan Bowser of Haynes Boone discusses the Federal Circuit's rejection of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board's "ministerial" standard for determining when a prior art patent can claim an earlier filing date under the America Invents Act.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Bowser
item.content:encoded: A backdating Issue The scenario recurs often. An inter partes review petitioner wants to use a patent or published application as prior art, but the reference's own filing date is too late. The reference, however, claims priority to a provisional or parent application filed before the challenged patent's effective filing date. If the reference can reach back to that earlier date, it becomes prior art. If it cannot, the petitioner's invalidity ground collapses. Patent claims are governed under the AIA if they have an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013. Patent claims with an effective filing date before March 16, 2013, are governed under pre-AIA law. Under pre-AIA law, the requirement for proving a reference patent is entitled to the earlier date of its provisional is governed by the Federal Circuit's decision in Dynamic Drinkware, LLC v. National Graphics, Inc., 800 F.3d 1375 (Fed. Cir. 2015). Under Dynamic Drinkware, a reference patent is entitled to its provisional's date only if (1) the provisional provides written description support under 35 U.S.C. § 112 for at least one claim of the reference patent, and (2) the subject matter relied upon in the reference patent is described in the provisional. The rationale was straightforward. A challenger should not be able to backdate prior art by claiming priority from an application that would not itself have supported a patent on the claimed invention. The Board's Penumbra framework In Penumbra, Inc. v. RapidPulse, Inc., IPR2021-01466, 2023 WL 2605070 (P.T.A.B. March 10, 2023), the Board held that Dynamic Drinkware's claim-support requirement was a product of pre-AIA § 102(e) and does not govern prior art determinations under AIA § 102. Instead, the Board announced a two-part test. A reference patent need only satisfy the "ministerial requirements" of AIA §§ 119 and 120 — a proper benefit claim, co-pendency, common inventorship — and the earlier application must "describe the subject matter" relied upon in the reference as prior art. Whether any claim of the reference was actually entitled to priority, the Board said, is not at issue. That framework did not emerge from nowhere. The Board leaned on the AIA's structural distinction between the "effective filing date" of a claimed invention under § 100(i) and the date a reference is "effectively filed" for prior art purposes under § 102(d). It also relied heavily on USPTO guidance, including MPEP § 2154.01(b) and a 2018 memorandum to the examining corps stating that the Dynamic Drinkware claim-support requirement "is not applicable when examining an application subject to the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA." Penumbra was designated precedential, and the Board applied it routinely — including in the IPR on appeal in Dental Monitoring, where the Board treated the reference patent as prior art as of its provisional date without deciding whether the provisional described any of the reference patent's claims. The statute supplies the answer The Federal Circuit based its decision in Dental Monitoring SAS v. Align Technology, Inc., 184 F.4th 1376 (Fed. Cir. 2026), on the text of the AIA. Section 102(d)(2) gives a reference the benefit of an earlier filing date only "if the patent or application for patent is entitled to claim a right of priority under [§] 119." Section 119(e)(1), in turn, extends entitlement to provisional priority only where the invention is "disclosed [in the provisional] in the manner provided by [§] 112(a)." Section 102(d) therefore incorporates a substantive written description requirement, and nothing in its text carves out prior art determinations or supplies a "less demanding 'ministerial' standard." The Court placed particular weight on the words "entitled to claim." That phrasing, it explained, refers to substantive entitlement, not the procedural act of asserting priority. Congress could have written § 102(d)(2) to cover a patent that merely "claims" or "asserts" a right of priority. It did not, and reading the provision the Board's way would render "entitled to" superfluous. The Court also corrected a persistent misreading of Dynamic Drinkware. Align argued that the decision was confined to pre-AIA § 102(e). But Dynamic Drinkware's footnote declining to address "newly designated § 102(d)" was a reservation of decision, not a holding that the AIA abrogated the written description requirement. The court noted that Align "confuses a reservation of decision with a holding on the merits." Even assuming Dynamic Drinkware does not formally control, the underlying principle survives: a reference cannot obtain the benefit of an earlier filing date for subject matter the earlier application did not support. As for § 100(i), the Court agreed that the AIA distinguishes an invention's effective filing date from a reference's effective prior art date, but held that the distinction "identifies which statutory inquiry is being performed" without telling us what substantive requirements "entitled" incorporates. And the Board's statements describing § 102(d) as imposing only "ministerial" requirements could not carry the day, because "the authoritative statement is the statutory text, not the legislative history." Because the Board never made the necessary factual findings, the court vacated and remanded rather than reversing, leaving the written description question for the Board in the first instance. A word on Rule 36 Practitioners who had treated Penumbra as blessed by the Federal Circuit should note a pointed footnote. The Court had earlier affirmed Penumbra by Rule 36 judgment without opinion.RapidPulse, Inc. v. Penumbra Inc., Nos. 2024-1130 and 2024-1131, 2025 WL 2911056 (Oct. 14, 2025). That affirmance, the Court explained, establishes only that the judgment below was correct; it "does not endorse or reject any specific part of the [Board's] reasoning," and "has no precedential value." A Rule 36 win is not an endorsement of the reasoning that produced it. Takeaways Petitioners bear a new burden of proof for prior art reference patents challenging AIA patents. Any ground resting on a reference patent's provisional or parent filing date now requires an affirmative showing that the earlier application provides § 112(a) written description support for at least one of the reference's published claims. That is a claim-by-claim, four-corners analysis — not a citation to the benefit claim on the reference's face. Petitions should build that record up front, with expert support, because the petitioner has the burden of persuasion to establish that a reference patent qualifies as prior art. Patent owners gain a powerful gatekeeping argument. Where the petition is silent on claim support, patent owners can attack the reference's prior art status directly, without engaging the merits of the obviousness theory. In closely spaced priority contests, that argument may be dispositive. Finally, the decision is a reminder about the durability of PTAB precedent. A precedential PTAB decision built substantially on agency guidance and legislative history is vulnerable when the statutory text points the other way — and a Rule 36 affirmance will not insulate it. Jonathan Bowser is a regular contributing columnist on patent law for Reuters Legal News and Westlaw Today.

item.title: Glencore shares to start trading in Australia as miner hopes to boost valuation
item.description: Glencore's , shares are set to start trading on the Australian Securities Exchange on Wednesday as the miner and trader hopes to secure a better valuation from Australia's mining-friendly investors who are seeking greater exposure to copper.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Glencore's (GLEN.L) , shares are set to start trading on the Australian Securities Exchange on Wednesday as the miner and trader hopes to secure a better valuation from Australia's mining-friendly investors who are seeking greater exposure to copper. Glencore CEO Gary Nagle expects strong demand from investors betting on copper's role in [USN:L8N45U2BV TEXT:"electrification"], he said on Friday, as demand rises for the metal's use in power grid upgrades, transport and AI data centres. The Switzerland-based company's CHESS Depository Interests (CDIs) will trade in a market home to other large miners like BHP Group (BHP.AX) , Rio Tinto (RIO.AX) , (RIO.L) and Fortescue (FMG.AX) . Glencore shares already trade in London and Johannesburg. Nagle has previously said he believes the $88 billion company can achieve inclusion in Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index (.AXJO) within 12 months, but analysts see momentum behind the stock potentially propelling it into the top indexes in [USN:L4N3Z11V1 TEXT:"half that time"]. Analysts and investors speculated Glencore's decision to list Down Under could help acclimatise those [USN:L8N44B03D TEXT:"who had not seen value"] in its approach to Rio Tinto last year. Rio Tinto walked away from takeover talks with Glencore in February, ending months of negotiations over a $240 billion tie-up that would have reshaped the global mining industry. Nagle told reporters last week that a deeper local presence in Australia, where it produces coal, copper, zinc, lead and nickel, may [USN:L8N45U2BV TEXT:"yield business opportunities"], although it had no set buyout list. JPMorgan analysts said on Friday after a meeting with Nagle that Glencore's management team still saw merits in a combination with Rio Tinto and noted its shares had outperformed its Anglo-Australian rival by 10% since negotiations collapsed in February. "M&A is seen as part of the growth strategy and it was noted 'who knows what happens in the future,'" the analysts said in a report.

item.title: US Supreme Court denies bid for pretrial release by anti-ICE activist
item.description: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to allow the pretrial release of an anti-ICE activist whose arrest for an allegedly threatening social media post during an immigration crackdown in Minneapolis was touted by President Donald Trump's administration in its campaign against "left-wing agitators."
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to allow the pretrial release of an anti-ICE activist whose arrest for an allegedly threatening social media post during an immigration crackdown in Minneapolis was touted by President Donald Trump 's administration in its campaign against "left-wing agitators." The justices denied self-described antifa, or "anti-fascist," member Kyle Wagner's request to revive a judge's ruling that ordered his pretrial release. Wagner was returned to custody after federal prosecutors appealed the judge's release order, arguing that he posed a danger to the community. Wagner's lawyers argued in court papers that he was being unlawfully detained and noted that he has no violent criminal history. Trump has made countering left-wing groups — and antifa in particular — a priority during his second term in office. The Republican president signed an executive order last year declaring the movement a "domestic terrorist organization" and has threatened to investigate and prosecute those who financially support it. Wagner faces one count each of cyberstalking and transmitting interstate threats for his attempt to publish personal information, or "dox," a prominent online supporter of Trump's hardline immigration policies. Prosecutors cited other social media posts by Wagner — including his statement that the situation in Minneapolis was "kill or be killed" — as evidence of his dangerousness. Wagner's arrest in Minneapolis on February 5 came during the Trump administration's large deployment of federal agents to the region in an immigration crackdown that spurred protests and led to the killing of two US citizens by immigration agents. During a White House briefing that day, then-White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt displayed a printed photograph of a shirtless Wagner — who has tattoos on his face, neck and chest — and described him to reporters as a "domestic terrorist." "As for the left-wing agitators who have been illegally obstructing ICE's immigration efforts, we are not letting that behavior go unnoticed or unpunished," Leavitt said from the White House lectern. "In fact, just today, the Department of Homeland Security arrested this individual. He is a self-proclaimed antifa member who has been threatening, doxing, harassing ICE." In August, the Cincinnati-based 6th US Circuit Court of Appeals granted the Justice Department's request to reverse US District Judge Denise Page Hood's pretrial release order. Wagner's trial is scheduled to begin in January. Judge Whitney Hermandorfer, a Trump appointee, wrote the 6th Circuit's 2-1 ruling that was joined by Judge Alan Norris, an appointee of Republican former President Ronald Reagan. The 6th Circuit ruled that the administration had made an adequate showing of Wagner's dangerousness. In dissent was Judge Rachel Bloomekatz, an appointee of Democratic former President Joe Biden, who wrote that, "The government seldom appeals pretrial release orders, so why is it insistent here?" Bloomekatz continued, "Wagner, who identifies as 'antifa' (anti-fascist) and has large tattoos on his face, neck and chest, looks aggressive in his social media videos, so it is no surprise that the White House press secretary held up a photo from one of his videos while touting law enforcement efforts against 'left-wing agitators.' ... But Wagner has never committed a violent crime." In his Supreme Court filing, Wagner's lawyers told the justices that the 6th Circuit's conclusion about his dangerousness was based on a "tendentious reading of Wagner's social media postings."

item.title: Fed's Collins sees another rate hike on the table before end of 2026
item.description: Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins said on Tuesday she believes the US central bank will need to raise interest rates again before the end of this year to lower high inflation.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins said on Tuesday she believes the US central bank will need to raise interest rates again before the end of this year to lower high inflation. Collins said she backed the rate hike by the central bank's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee last month and currently expects "it will be appropriate to raise rates a bit further before the end of the year to ensure a timely and durable return of inflation to the Committee's 2% target." "My view of the need for further policy action, and the appropriate timing, will depend importantly on how the totality of incoming data shapes my outlook and the associated balance of risks," she said in the text of a speech to be delivered at a banking conference at the Boston Fed. Collins said that with the economy and job market doing well, the Fed can focus its work on bringing inflation back down to its target after missing that goal for more than five years. The Fed raised its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range last month. Policymaker forecasts released at that meeting penciled in another increase by the end of 2026, although a range of Fed officials have in recent weeks [USN:S0N44V01O TEXT:"strongly suggested"] the move will come in December and not at the October 27-28 meeting. Collins was largely upbeat about the economic outlook, though she acknowledged there were risks. The "most likely" path "continues to feature healthy GDP growth, with the labor market remaining near full employment," she said. "In this scenario, inflation gradually returns to 2%, as continued efficiency gains support the balance between demand and supply, and contribute to disinflation." But pressure from tech investment to build AI infrastructure and the ongoing impact of tariffs and energy costs driven by the war in the Middle East could complicate the effort to lower inflation, she said. "I expect both total and core inflation to again run above the Fed's 2% target in the coming months, given the recent jump in prices of refined energy products like jet and diesel fuel, and home heating oil," Collins added.

item.title: Saudi OpenAI engineer arrested by FBI over hidden recording device, US DOJ says
item.description: US federal agents arrested a Saudi national employed as an OpenAI engineer and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company, the Justice Department said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US federal agents arrested a Saudi national employed as an OpenAI engineer and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company, the Justice Department said on Tuesday. OpenAI had used its internal AI models to identify the individual responsible for planting the device and to trace its origins, it said in an X post . "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated," according to the AI company. The company said it referred the matter to the FBI, which is continuing to investigate. The FBI did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for more details. Earlier this year, a Texas man [USN:L4N40W1SN TEXT:"was charged with "]throwing a Molotov cocktail at the home of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and attempting to set fire to the AI firm's headquarters. OpenAI faces scrutiny over security incidents involving its AI systems. Reuters and other media outlets reported recently that [USN:L6N45U1FJ TEXT:"the company had told investors"] its annualized revenue for September was almost $50 billion, a drop from what it signaled earlier. OpenAI said on Friday it fired [USN:L6N45V0B0 TEXT:"three researchers "]after an investigation found they had violated company policies on handling sensitive information. The statement came after the researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, published a letter detailing the circumstances of their dismissal and arguing that the abrupt firings could create uncertainty among employees and undermine a culture that had allowed researchers to raise safety concerns.

item.title: Uber gets green light to pursue racketeering case against Philadelphia lawyer
item.description: Uber Technologies can pursue civil racketeering claims against a Philadelphia-based lawyer even though the company's insurer footed its defense bills in a series of allegedly fraudulent personal injury lawsuits, a federal judge ruled on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: Uber Technologies (UBER.N) can pursue civil racketeering claims against a Philadelphia-based lawyer even though the company's insurer footed its defense bills in a series of allegedly fraudulent personal injury lawsuits, a federal judge ruled on Tuesday. US District Judge Mark Kearney in Philadelphia held that the rideshare giant has standing to pursue its case against Marc Simon and his firm Simon & Simon. Uber alleges the law firm worked with doctors and other providers to file fraudulent personal injury claims against it and Federal Express Corporation (FDX.N) . Simon and his firm have denied wrongdoing. "Uber did not relinquish its standing to sue parties who bring fraudulent claims against it by purchasing liability insurance and permitting its conduit, Farmers, to issue payments on its behalf," Kearney wrote in his 14-page ruling . An Uber spokesperson said in a statement that Kearney's ruling "makes clear that Uber can continue pursuing its racketeering claims, and we remain confident in our case." A spokesperson for Simon & Simon did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The case is scheduled to go to trial in March. Uber and FedEx have mounted similar lawsuits against law firms in federal courts in [USN:L1N3TI014 TEXT:"Los Angeles"], [USN:L6N3SE0TU TEXT:"Miami"] and [USN:L6N40R0DN TEXT:"New York"] alleging lawyers worked in conjunction with medical providers to file bogus and exaggerated claims against them. Kearney in May [USN:L6N41O15M TEXT:"denied a motion to dismiss"] Uber and FedEx's case against the Simon & Simon firm. The companies alleged Simon directs clients to certain providers whose unnecessary treatments or false diagnoses inflate the value of their claims, which could result in a larger settlement. FedEx and Uber claim that Simon and his firm direct these medical providers to create fraudulent documents which are then used as the basis of litigation. Simon has argued that the companies are abusing RICO in an effort to put him out of business. He brought [USN:L6N42H0ZU TEXT:"counterclaims"] against Uber and FedEx in June, asserting their RICO allegations are "objectively and subjectively baseless" because some cases they agreed to settle were being cited as evidence of a racketeering scheme. Kearney dismissed the counterclaims in August.

item.title: Lufthansa set to win bidding for stake in Portugal's TAP, SIC reports
item.description: Germany's Lufthansa is set to win the bidding for the purchase of a 44.9% stake in Portugal's flag carrier TAP over rival Air France-KLM , broadcaster SIC said on Tuesday, citing sources familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany's Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) is set to win the bidding for the purchase of a 44.9% stake in Portugal's flag carrier TAP over rival Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) , broadcaster SIC said on Tuesday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The German group is offering an all-cash deal for its stake in TAP, unlike Air France-KLM, whose proposal combines cash and shares in the Franco-Dutch airline, SIC reported. Lufthansa's stronger financial position was also a key factor, it added. Portugal's Infrastructure Ministry declined to comment. Air France-KLM and Lufthansa submitted final bids for the stake in [USN:L1N44W0H6 TEXT:"September"] after Portugal's government requested both bidders improve their offers. The government is due to choose the winner at an extraordinary cabinet meeting on Wednesday.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, dijo el martes que propuso celebrar nuevas conversaciones en los próximos días con los enviados estadounidenses Steve Witkoff y Jared Kushner, en un momento en que Washington intensifica sus esfuerzos para que Kiev y Moscú vuelvan a la mesa de negociaciones. La propuesta surge tras las conversaciones mantenidas la semana pasada en Estados Unidos, en las que Witkoff y Kushner comunicaron a una delegación ucraniana que un acuerdo que permitiera las exportaciones rusas de gasóleo tenía como objetivo hacer que Moscú volviera a la mesa de negociaciones. En su discurso nocturno por video, Zelenski también afirmó que Ucrania apoyaba la tregua energética propuesta por el presidente Donald Trump, siempre y cuando Rusia la respetara. "Nuestro equipo ha enviado a la parte estadounidense las propuestas pertinentes sobre posibles próximas reuniones y conversaciones. En los próximos días, estamos dispuestos a reunirnos y he transmitido esta propuesta a Steve Witkoff y Jared Kushner a través de mi equipo".

item.title: Atlanta Dream to host WNBA Finals Games 3 and 4 at home of NBA's Hawks
item.description: The Atlanta Dream will move Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries to the larger home of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks in a bid to accommodate more fans, the Dream and Hawks said in a joint statement on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Dream will move Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries to the larger home of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks in a bid to accommodate more fans, the Dream and Hawks said in a joint statement on Tuesday. The switch required several scheduling changes because the original date for Game 3 clashed with a concert at the arena, while the Hawks host the Houston Rockets there on the day of Game 4. Game 3 has therefore been brought forward by a day to October 21. Game 4 will still be played on October 24 but with an earlier tip-off so as not to clash with the Hawks game. "This is what the players and the fans deserve," Larry Gottesdiener, Atlanta Dream majority owner, said in a news release. "We are grateful to all of the stakeholders who worked together to resolve the conflicts and make this happen." The Dream, who have played home games in recent seasons at a 3,500-seat venue, announced last week that they would move to the Hawks' arena next year under a multi-year agreement.
